analysis: The trial succeeded with host validation macro HR@10 of 0.515, improving by 0.0163 over ConvRec (0.4987) and 0.010 over SASRec (0.505). Per-category HR@10: Movies_and_TV 0.565, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.570, Electronics 0.355, CDs_and_Vinyl 0.570. Electronics remained weak, below the reported ConvRec 0.360 and SASRec 0.420. The aggregate result supports retaining the scaled attention variant for further controlled experiments, but does not establish that adaptive retrieval or residual scaling caused the improvement. No test results were available.
code_summary: One jointly trained ConvRec per category: 96-dimensional tied item embeddings, learned item bias, four causal convolutional residual blocks with dilations 1/2/4/8, then pre-normalized two-head causal attention with dropout 0.25 and a trainable residual scale initialized to 0.1, followed by final LayerNorm. Attention masks future positions and padding, with safe handling of empty histories. Training preserves 256-negative sampled softmax, a 2048-token cap, unweighted token reduction, AdamW, seed 42, and strict validation HR@10 checkpoint selection. Prefix sampling mixes terminal windows and random endpoints equally. The generated predictor strictly loads exactly one selected checkpoint per category; checks cover finite outputs/gradients, zero padded features, causality, and predictor score agreement. No ensembles or separately fitted scorers.
